Observed audience-language patterns for one-person-company founders:
- They describe the pain as "I keep switching between selling, researching, following up, and actually doing the work."
- "AI manager" is often read as another dashboard or advisor unless the copy makes clear that work is actually carried through.

Messaging package — founder review draft (v7)

Status
Review only. This bounded draft is for founder review; it has not been sent or published.

Launch scope
Relaunch messaging for one-person-company founders, with lean-SME operators as a secondary audience. The launch goal is to improve recognition and signup conversion. Current internal signal: low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves.

Core audience
Primary: one-person-company founders who personally move between selling, researching, following up, and doing the work.
Secondary: lean-SME operators who remain close to day-to-day operations.

Positioning
Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs. It is positioned as operating support for people carrying the recurring demands of running a business—not as a generic dashboard, and not as a claim of unsupervised autonomy.

Core message
Run the business with support that fits the way one-person companies actually work. Somebody helps extend what a one-person company can do by supporting the operator across the work of running the business.

Proposed launch-facing page copy

Headline
The AI manager for your one-person company.

Subheadline
Somebody helps you carry the work of running your business—from selling and researching to following up and getting the work done.

Primary CTA
See how Somebody can support your business

Supporting copy
You are not just doing one job. You are moving between finding opportunities, understanding what matters, following up, and delivering the work. Somebody is built for one-person companies and lean SMEs that need broader operating support without losing sight of the day-to-day.

For founders who do the work themselves
Somebody is designed for the reality of running a one-person company: many responsibilities, limited time, and no separate team for every task. It extends what you can do by helping you carry work across the recurring demands of operating the business.

What this message deliberately does
- Names one-person-company founders directly so visitors can recognise themselves.
- Describes the product as an AI manager, consistent with the company profile.
- Uses support and extend language rather than promising autonomous execution or specific unverified capabilities.
- Connects the message to the observed recognition and signup-conversion problem.

Claim guardrails
Supported by supplied company records: Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs; the company aims to extend what a one-person company can do; the relaunch targets one-person-company founders and addresses low signup conversion and weak visitor recognition.
Do not add claims about guaranteed results, specific integrations, autonomous actions, time saved, revenue generated, customer counts, or verified feature behavior unless separately confirmed by the product owner.

Review checklist before launch
1. Founder/product owner verifies that “helps you carry the work” accurately describes currently available behavior.
2. Founder/product owner confirms the primary CTA and any signup flow wording.
3. Keep this package in review status until approved; do not send or publish from this draft.
4. After approval, compare against the current generic copy before publishing.

Source note
Draft based on company records: Launch context and goals (launch/context) and Company profile (company/profile).

<untrusted_content source="company_artifact:launch/page-message" origin="bounded_draft">
Messaging diagnosis — review draft (v2)

Scope and evidence
- Current launch copy: “Somebody: an AI manager for your business.” / “Automate your workflows with AI.” The supplied status says the launch is not converting; visitors leave without signing up. The stated audience is generic “businesses,” and the stated pain is “too many tools.”
- Proprietary audience-language input (resultEvidenceId: sim_result_9c1330d5883c771d00505368) reports patterns for one-person-company founders: switching among selling, researching, following up, and doing the work; “AI manager” can be read as another dashboard/advisor unless execution is explicit; concrete outcome/accountability language is easier to understand than generic workflow-automation language.
- Public-web observation (https://somebody.ai; result label ev_1790029327188_drepe6) shows the URL as a domain-for-sale page, not product messaging. Therefore current public positioning, product proof, and audience fit cannot be independently evaluated from that URL.

Principal messaging problems, ranked by likely impact
1. Unclear outcome and execution promise — HIGH likely impact.
   Evidence: The headline names a category (“AI manager”) without stating what gets finished. The subhead says “Automate your workflows,” which the proprietary input describes as broad/tool-like; the same input says founders want an accountable system that notices missing capability, gets what it needs, does the work, and returns with a finished result.
   Risk/uncertainty: “Likely impact” is a prioritization judgment, not a measured causal finding. No A/B or funnel data was supplied.

2. Audience is too broad — HIGH likely impact.
   Evidence: The current page assumes generic “businesses,” while the proprietary input specifically identifies one-person-company founders and their job-switching pain. The copy does not name that audience or situation.
   Unsupported assumption: The one-person-company founder segment is a promising candidate, not proven to be the only or best segment. Segment size, willingness to pay, and conversion by segment are unknown.

3. Category language may create the wrong mental model — MEDIUM–HIGH likely impact.
   Evidence: “AI manager” can be interpreted as a dashboard or advisor unless the copy makes clear that work is carried through (proprietary input). The supplied headline offers no explicit finished-work/result language.
   Unsupported assumption: This interpretation is reported as an audience-language pattern, not a universal response; no direct interview or experiment results were supplied.

4. Pain framing centers “too many tools” rather than the operating burden — MEDIUM likely impact.
   Evidence: The supplied page assumes “too many tools,” while the proprietary input reports the more concrete pain of repeatedly switching between selling, researching, following up, and doing the work. The current message does not describe that burden.
   Uncertainty: The supplied materials do not establish whether tool overload or role-switching is the stronger conversion driver.

5. Insufficient public proof/context — MEDIUM confidence as a diagnosis, not necessarily a copy defect.
   Evidence: The supplied public URL currently resolves to a domain-for-sale page (ev_1790029327188_drepe6), so public visitors/reviewers cannot use it to validate product positioning or capabilities.
   Material limitation: This observation does not prove why the launch is not converting and does not establish product performance. It may reflect a stale or incorrect URL rather than the intended launch page.

Recommended messaging direction for review (not published)
- Lead with the founder’s desired outcome and accountability: one system that takes ownership of a job and returns a finished result.
- Name the initial audience and concrete operating burden, subject to validation: one-person-company founders who are switching among selling, research, follow-up, and delivery.
- Explain “make-versus-buy” capability underneath the outcome rather than leading with “AI manager” or generic workflow automation.
- Validate with message testing and funnel evidence before treating any ranking as causal.

Candidate review copy (hypothesis, not approved claim)
Headline: “Get the work finished—not another AI dashboard.”
Subhead: “Somebody helps one-person-company founders move from selling and research to follow-up and delivery by taking ownership of the job and returning with a finished result.”
Qualification: This wording is a test hypothesis derived from supplied evidence, not a verified product claim. Confirm actual capabilities, target segment, and proof before use.
</untrusted_content>

Messaging proposal — review draft (v3)

Purpose
A proposed relaunch message for review only. This is a bounded draft; it is not published or sent.

Audience
One-person-company founders and lean-SME operators who personally move between selling, researching, following up, and delivering the work. Lead with “one-person company” rather than generic “business” so visitors can recognise themselves.

Diagnosed problem addressed
The current signal is low signup conversion because visitors do not recognise themselves. Existing language—“an AI manager for your business” and “Automate your workflows with AI”—is broad, describes a category rather than a concrete outcome, and may make “AI manager” sound like another dashboard or advisor. The proposal therefore names the operator, the day-to-day workload, and the intended outcome without claiming capabilities that have not been verified.

Value proposition
Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs, intended to help the operator keep important business work moving across selling, research, follow-up, and delivery. The value is less context switching and clearer accountability for the work that needs to happen next—subject to confirmation of the product’s actual execution capabilities.

Positioning
For founders running a business largely on their own, Somebody is an AI manager focused on keeping business work moving—not generic workflow automation and not merely another dashboard. This positioning is a candidate for review and testing; the product experience must substantiate any execution or accountability language before publication.

Core message (candidate)
“Running a one-person company means switching between selling, research, follow-up, and delivery. Somebody is your AI manager for keeping the work moving—so you can spend less time coordinating what needs to happen next and more time building the business.”

Supporting message options
- “For founders doing the selling, research, follow-up, and delivery themselves.”
- “Turn the work in your head into a clearer next step.”
- “An AI manager for one-person companies—not generic automation.”

Suggested call to action
“See how it works” or “Join the relaunch” (choose only after confirming the actual signup/onboarding flow). Avoid promising autonomous completion unless that capability is verified.

Supportable claims and guardrails
- Supportable from supplied company records: Somebody is built as an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs; the relaunch goal is to convert one-person-company founders.
- Supportable as a messaging diagnosis: current conversion is low and visitors do not recognise themselves; explicit audience language is therefore warranted.
- Use “intended to,” “helps,” or “keeps work moving” until product behavior is verified.
- Do not claim guaranteed conversion, autonomous execution, completed tasks, measurable time savings, or universal workflow automation. Do not imply that the public site currently validates the proposition: the supplied public URL could not independently substantiate product messaging.

Review and test plan
Before publishing, confirm the product can deliver the promised experience, then test this audience-specific, outcome/accountability-led draft against the current generic copy. Measure signup conversion and whether visitors can identify the intended audience and explain the product’s value. Keep this artifact as a review draft until those checks are complete.

Sources used for this draft
- Company record: launch/context (relaunch goal, low signup conversion, visitor-recognition problem, owned resources and publishing constraint).
- Company record: company/profile (Somebody’s product description and target company size).
- Existing v2 review draft and its cited supplied evidence (current copy, diagnosed messaging problems, founder-language patterns, and public URL limitation).

Messaging package — founder review draft (v4)

Status
Review only. This package is a bounded draft for founder review and launch use after approval; it has not been sent or published.

Launch scope
Relaunch messaging for one-person-company founders and lean-SME operators. The immediate goal is to make the intended audience recognise themselves and improve signup conversion. Lead with “one-person company” rather than generic “business.”

Primary audience
You run a one-person company or lean SME and personally move between selling, researching, following up, and delivering the work. You need important business work to keep moving without losing track of what needs attention.

Core positioning
Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.

Recommended hero
Eyebrow: For one-person companies
Headline: Keep the work that runs your business moving.
Subheadline: Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs—helping you stay on top of selling, research, follow-up, and delivery in one place.
Primary CTA: Try Somebody
Secondary CTA: See how it works
Support line: Built for founders who are doing the work themselves.

Problem / recognition section
You are selling, researching, following up, and delivering—often in the same day. When every task depends on you, important work can stall between the next conversation, the next decision, and the next delivery.

How Somebody is described
Use: “Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.” Explain the intended role as helping the operator keep important business work moving across selling, research, follow-up, and delivery.
Do not describe Somebody as a human employee, autonomous replacement, guaranteed revenue generator, or a product that completes unverified actions. Do not promise specific integrations, automation, outcomes, response times, or workflow execution unless the product owner confirms them.

Benefits to communicate
• See the work that needs attention across selling, research, follow-up, and delivery.
• Spend less time switching context between the responsibilities you carry yourself.
• Keep accountability clearer for the next important piece of work.
These are intended benefits of the positioning, not quantified or guaranteed results.

Suggested supporting copy
One-person companies do not have separate teams for every function. Somebody is designed around the reality that the founder is moving the business forward across multiple kinds of work. Use it to frame the work that needs to happen and decide what deserves attention next.

CTA and conversion guidance
Primary CTA: Try Somebody.
Alternative CTA for experiments: Start with your work.
CTA copy must be paired with the actual signup flow and current product availability. Do not imply a free trial, free tier, immediate access, or a particular onboarding experience unless confirmed.

FAQ / objection handling
Who is Somebody for?
Somebody is positioned for one-person-company founders and lean-SME operators who personally handle work across selling, research, follow-up, and delivery.
What does “AI manager” mean here?
It is the product’s positioning: a way to help the operator keep important business work moving. Confirm the concrete capabilities before adding feature-level claims.
Will Somebody do the work for me?
Do not promise that. The launch message should describe support for keeping work moving, not replacement of the operator or guaranteed autonomous execution.

Claim guardrails
Approved from supplied material: the company builds Somebody; it is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs; the relaunch is aimed at one-person-company founders; current signal is low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves; the message should address selling, research, follow-up, and delivery.
Unverified and excluded: quantified performance, revenue or time savings, guaranteed conversion improvement, autonomous task completion, specific integrations, pricing, free access, security/compliance claims, customer results, and availability promises.

Founder review checklist
1. Confirm the hero language and primary CTA.
2. Confirm the actual capabilities behind “AI manager” and the four work areas.
3. Confirm the signup flow and any access, pricing, or trial language before use.
4. Remove or revise any line that implies an unverified feature or outcome.
5. After approval, test this audience-specific package against the current generic copy; do not publish from this draft without founder approval.

Source basis
Company profile: Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.
Launch context and goals: relaunch for one-person-company founders; current low signup conversion and weak audience recognition.

Messaging package — founder review draft (v5)

Status
Review only. This bounded draft is for founder review; it has not been sent or published.

Launch scope
Relaunch messaging for one-person-company founders and lean-SME operators. The immediate goal is to improve audience recognition and signup conversion.

Evidence basis
- Company record: launch/context — the current internal signal is low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves.
- Supplied audience-language evidence (simulated proprietary social evidence, resultEvidenceId sim_result_9c1330d5883c771d00505368) — founders describe switching between selling, researching, following up, and doing the work; “AI manager” can be read as another dashboard or advisor unless the copy makes clear that work is carried through; concrete outcome/accountability language is easier to understand than generic workflow-automation language.

Principal messaging problems, ranked by likely impact

1. Audience recognition is insufficient — HIGH likely impact
Evidence: launch/context reports low signup conversion and that visitors do not recognise themselves. The page should explicitly name one-person-company founders and the work they personally juggle. This is a prioritisation based on the current signal, not a proven causal diagnosis.

2. “AI manager” may signal advice or another dashboard rather than completed work — HIGH likely impact
Evidence: supplied audience-language evidence says this interpretation is common unless copy makes clear that work is actually carried through. Current positioning uses “AI manager,” so it needs an outcome/accountability explanation alongside the category label. Unsupported assumption: this applies to the whole target audience and is not yet validated by a controlled message test.

3. The value proposition may be too broad or tool-like — MEDIUM-HIGH likely impact
Evidence: supplied audience-language evidence says generic “automate your workflows” language feels broad, while concrete language about owning an outcome and finishing the job is easier to understand. Avoid claiming workflow automation as the primary benefit unless product capability and performance are confirmed.

4. The message may describe activities without making the promised handoff/result concrete — MEDIUM likely impact
Evidence: supplied audience-language evidence identifies the desired outcome as one accountable system that can notice missing capability, get what it needs, do the work, and return with a finished result. Treat this as directional audience evidence, not proof that the product currently delivers every part of that sequence.

Recommended messaging direction for review
Lead with the founder’s outcome and accountability, then explain the make-versus-buy capability underneath. Prefer concrete language about keeping a business task moving and returning with a finished result, while retaining explicit guardrails against unverified feature or outcome claims.

- No baseline signup-conversion rate, sample size, segment breakdown, or experiment result is supplied.

history.content:
Messaging package — founder review draft (v6)

Status
Review only. This bounded draft is for founder review; it has not been sent or published.

Purpose and diagnosed problems addressed
The relaunch is intended to improve recognition and signup conversion among one-person-company founders. The current internal signal is low signup conversion and that visitors do not recognise themselves. This draft addresses that diagnosis by naming the audience directly, explaining the product in outcome-oriented language, distinguishing Somebody from a generic dashboard or advisor, and keeping claims limited to what the supplied material supports.

Audience
Primary: one-person-company founders who personally move between selling, researching, following up, and doing the work.
Secondary: lean-SME operators who need broader operating support but are still close to the day-to-day work.

Value proposition
Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs. The proposed value is to extend what a one-person company can do by helping the operator carry work across the recurring demands of running the business, rather than presenting only another tool or dashboard.

Positioning
For founders who are the person responsible for both growing and operating the business, Somebody is an AI manager that helps them handle more of the work involved in running it. Unlike generic workflow-automation or dashboard language, this positioning makes the intended audience and practical operating role explicit. It should not imply human employment, guaranteed results, autonomous execution beyond verified capability, or a specific feature that has not been confirmed.

Core message
You run the business. Somebody helps you run more of it.

Supporting message
For one-person-company founders and lean-SME operators juggling selling, researching, following up, and doing the work: Somebody is an AI manager built to extend what you can do. See whether it fits the way you run your business.

Proposed page copy
Headline
You run the business. Somebody helps you run more of it.

Subhead
An AI manager for one-person-company founders and lean-SME operators who are selling, researching, following up, and doing the work themselves.

Recognition line
If you are the person moving the business forward and keeping the work moving, this is for you.

CTA
See how Somebody fits your business

Supportable claims and guardrails
- Supportable from company material: Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs.
- Supportable from company material: the product is intended to extend what a one-person company can do.
- Supportable as a relaunch objective, not a product-performance claim: the copy is designed to improve audience recognition and signup conversion.
- Directional wording only: “helps you run more of it” describes the proposed positioning and must be checked against current capabilities before publication.
- Do not claim guaranteed conversion, revenue, time savings, autonomous completion of work, human-equivalent management, or particular integrations/features without separate verification.

Problem-to-message mapping
1. Visitors do not recognise themselves → name one-person-company founders and lean-SME operators in the headline/subhead and describe their day-to-day role.
2. “AI manager” may sound like another dashboard or advisor → pair the category label with the concrete operating context and “helps you run more of it,” without promising unverified autonomy.
3. Broad tool/workflow language is unclear → lead with the founder’s responsibility and the work they are already doing, not generic automation terminology.
4. Outcome language can overreach → use a bounded “helps” formulation and retain explicit capability verification before publication.

Evidence basis
- Company record: launch/context — the relaunch goal is to convert one-person-company founders; the current signal is low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves.
- Company record: company/profile — Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs; the company builds it to extend what a one-person company can do.
- Prior founder-review package (v5) and supplied audience-language evidence identified the need for explicit audience recognition, clearer distinction from a dashboard/advisor, concrete operating language, and cautious outcome wording. These remain directional inputs and are not treated as independently verified performance claims.

Review gate
Before sending or publishing, the founder or product owner should verify that the “helps you run more of it” wording matches current product capabilities and that the CTA and signup flow are aligned. This draft is not a publication or send instruction.

Messaging package — founder review draft (v7)

Status
Review only. This bounded draft is for founder review; it has not been sent or published.

Launch scope
Relaunch messaging for one-person-company founders, with lean-SME operators as a secondary audience. The launch goal is to improve recognition and signup conversion. Current internal signal: low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves.

Core audience
Primary: one-person-company founders who personally move between selling, researching, following up, and doing the work.
Secondary: lean-SME operators who remain close to day-to-day operations.

Positioning
Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs. It is positioned as operating support for people carrying the recurring demands of running a business—not as a generic dashboard, and not as a claim of unsupervised autonomy.

Core message
Run the business with support that fits the way one-person companies actually work. Somebody helps extend what a one-person company can do by supporting the operator across the work of running the business.

Proposed launch-facing page copy

Headline
The AI manager for your one-person company.

Subheadline
Somebody helps you carry the work of running your business—from selling and researching to following up and getting the work done.

Primary CTA
See how Somebody can support your business

Supporting copy
You are not just doing one job. You are moving between finding opportunities, understanding what matters, following up, and delivering the work. Somebody is built for one-person companies and lean SMEs that need broader operating support without losing sight of the day-to-day.

For founders who do the work themselves
Somebody is designed for the reality of running a one-person company: many responsibilities, limited time, and no separate team for every task. It extends what you can do by helping you carry work across the recurring demands of operating the business.

What this message deliberately does
- Names one-person-company founders directly so visitors can recognise themselves.
- Describes the product as an AI manager, consistent with the company profile.
- Uses support and extend language rather than promising autonomous execution or specific unverified capabilities.
- Connects the message to the observed recognition and signup-conversion problem.

Claim guardrails
Supported by supplied company records: Somebody is an AI manager for one-person companies and lean SMEs; the company aims to extend what a one-person company can do; the relaunch targets one-person-company founders and addresses low signup conversion and weak visitor recognition.
Do not add claims about guaranteed results, specific integrations, autonomous actions, time saved, revenue generated, customer counts, or verified feature behavior unless separately confirmed by the product owner.

Review checklist before launch
1. Founder/product owner verifies that “helps you carry the work” accurately describes currently available behavior.
2. Founder/product owner confirms the primary CTA and any signup flow wording.
3. Keep this package in review status until approved; do not send or publish from this draft.
4. After approval, compare against the current generic copy before publishing.

Source note
Draft based on company records: Launch context and goals (launch/context) and Company profile (company/profile).

objective.request: Our launch messaging isn’t working. Figure out what’s wrong and get a better relaunch ready. You can spend within the approved limit if it’s justified.
objective.title: Our launch messaging isn’t working. Figure out what’s wro…

outcome.intent: Identify the evidence-based causes of ineffective launch messaging and produce a materially improved, launch-ready relaunch messaging package.

levels.label: Diagnosis complete
levels.statement: The principal reasons the launch messaging is not working are identified, supported by relevant launch evidence, and distinguished from unsupported hypotheses.

levels.label: Relaunch specified
levels.statement: A revised messaging direction is defined that directly addresses the diagnosed failures and states the intended audience, promise, positioning, and supporting claims.

levels.label: Relaunch ready
levels.statement: A complete revised messaging package exists for the defined launch scope, is internally consistent, addresses the diagnosed failures, and is ready for founder review and launch use.

requirements.mustBeTrue: The available launch messaging, intended audience and offer context, and relevant evidence about launch performance and audience response are assembled and sufficiently reliable for diagnosis.
requirements.title: Relevant launch evidence is available

requirements.mustBeTrue: The principal messaging problems are identified, ranked by likely impact, and tied to evidence, with material uncertainties and unsupported assumptions clearly marked.
requirements.title: Messaging failure diagnosis is complete

requirements.mustBeTrue: The proposed relaunch messaging directly addresses the diagnosed problems and clearly defines the audience, value proposition, positioning, core message, and supportable claims.
requirements.title: Improved messaging direction is defined

requirements.mustBeTrue: A complete, coherent revised messaging package exists for the defined launch scope, is consistent with the approved offer and supportable claims, contains the required launch-facing message content, and is ready for founder review and launch use.
requirements.title: Relaunch messaging package is ready

workers.responsibility:
Retrieve the requested facts from company records and record them with their source. Report gaps instead of inferring missing values.
Draft the requested artifact from supplied material only, and leave it for review rather than sending or publishing it.
Research public sources and internal records as needed, update the controlled company artifact with a versioned change, and request any missing resources the application must acquire. Do not invoke providers, authorize spend, or make arbitrary external calls.
Answer the assigned question from public sources and record findings with their provenance. Do not assert anything the sources do not support.
